candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Handling Hazardous and Infectious Materials, printed p.25 / PDF p.29: follow procedures for handling biohazardous and hazardous materials; demonstrate safe handling techniques
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hazardous-drug contaminated waste disposal
candidate.educational_objective: Dispose of disposable PPE contaminated with hazardous antineoplastic drugs in the designated hazardous-drug waste stream according to facility and applicable regulatory procedures.

options.A: Place them in the facility's designated hazardous-drug waste container according to hazardous-drug disposal procedures
options.B: Place them in regular trash because they are disposable PPE rather than medication
options.C: Place them in an ordinary sharps container even though they contain no sharps
options.D: Rinse the disposable PPE in the sink before placing it in regular waste

candidate.rationale: OSHA hazardous-drug guidance identifies used gloves, gowns, and related disposable materials contaminated with hazardous drugs as hazardous-drug-related waste and recommends designated, labeled hazardous-drug waste bags and covered containers. Such contaminated PPE should not be placed in ordinary trash, an unrelated sharps container, or rinsed in a sink. Exact disposal requirements must also follow applicable federal, state, local, and facility rules. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Disposable PPE contaminated with hazardous drugs should enter a designated, labeled hazardous-drug waste stream rather than ordinary trash, with final disposal following applicable regulations and facility procedures.
candidate.source_document_title: Hospitals eTool — Pharmacy: Disposal of Hazardous Drugs
candidate.source_locator: Recognized Controls and Work Practices — Hazardous waste containers and disposal: use thick leak-proof plastic bags for discarded gloves, gowns and other related disposable material; clearly label bags as hazardous-drug-related waste; keep the bag in a covered container labeled for hazardous-drug waste; dispose according to applicable federal, state and local regulations
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Labor — Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
candidate.stem: After administering a hazardous antineoplastic drug, the nurse removes a disposable gown and chemotherapy gloves that are contaminated with the drug. How should these items be discarded?
